accounts.description: GitLab instances to talk to, keyed by the name watches refer to.

ui.description: Window and presentation settings, consumed by the GUI shell.

verdict.description: Optional replacement for the built-in icon-state rules.

watches.description: What to watch. Order is the display order.

Account.description: One GitLab instance and the credential used against it.

api_path.description: API prefix. Overridable for proxies that mount the API elsewhere.

base_url.description: Instance root, without a trailing slash, e.g. `https://gitlab.com`.

rate_limit_backoff.description: How far the poll interval is allowed to back off after rate limiting.

token.description: Where the token comes from. Never the token itself.

AuthHeader.description: The header spelling used to authenticate.

oneOf.description: `PRIVATE-TOKEN: <token>`, the GitLab personal/project access token form.
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`, for OAuth and CI job tokens.
The first failing job, falling back to the pipeline when green.
Always the pipeline.
The deploy marker job, falling back to the pipeline.
Not clickable.

DiveConfig.description: Which trigger jobs to walk into.

bridges.description:
Glob over trigger-job names. `"*"` dives into all of them; `""` into
none, which turns the watch into a cheap one-request-per-tick row.

depth.description:
How many levels of child pipeline to walk. `1` is the parent's own
children.

exclude.description: Trigger-job name globs to skip even when `bridges` matches them.

only_when.description:
Restrict diving to bridges in a given state, e.g. `"failed"`. This is
how a noisy secondary watch stays cheap until something breaks.

FailurePolicy.description: What a secondary failure does to an otherwise successful deploy.

oneOf.description: Deployed, but the icon says so with a warning overlay.
Treat it as an outright failure.
Do not let it affect the icon at all.

mode.description:
`auto` is a template image on macOS and the coloured set elsewhere;
`template` forces a macOS template image; `color` forces the coloured set.

states.description: Per-state glyph names, for themes that offer alternatives.

JobOverride.description: How a job's class is forced, regardless of its raw status.

oneOf.description: A manual job that should read as a gate rather than as missing work.
Demote a blocking failure to a warning.
Promote an allow-failure failure to blocking.
Hide the job from every verdict and from the rows.

JobOverrides.description: Job-name patterns (literal, or "re:<regex>") mapped to a forced class. Evaluated in file order; the first match wins.

JobsMode.description:
Which jobs a pipeline row lists when it is expanded.

Presentation only: the view model carries every job either way, so flipping
the mode redraws from what is already held instead of waiting for a fetch,
and the verdict never depends on it.

oneOf.description: Only the jobs the verdict names: failures, warnings and gates.
Every job, parent and child, grouped by stage. The 0.1.0 default.

LogConfig.description: Logging and the bounded request ring the debug pane reads.

keep_requests.description: How many recent HTTP requests to keep for the debug pane.

NotifyConfig.description: Which events notify, and what they say.

blocking_failure.description: A new blocking failure appeared, or a bridge lost its child.

body.description: MiniJinja template for the notification body.

finished.description: A pipeline reached a settled state.

gate_opened.description: A bridge parked at a manual gate.

title.description: MiniJinja template for the notification title.

idle_secs.description: Interval used when everything has settled.

live_secs.description: Interval used while anything relevant is unsettled.

hide_on_blur.description: Dismiss the popover when it loses focus.

max_height.description: Maximum height in logical pixels before the list scrolls.

ProjectRef.description: A project, addressed either by numeric id or by namespace path.

anyOf.description: Numeric project id, the cheapest and most stable form.

RateLimitBackoff.description:
How far the backoff is allowed to grow after repeated rate limiting or
server errors.

max_secs.description: Ceiling for the doubled interval, in seconds.

Role.description: Whether a watch drives the tray icon.

oneOf.description: Contributes to the tray icon state and may notify.

Contributes rows to the popover only. Never touches the icon, never
notifies. This is what keeps an hourly schedule that is red by design
out of the tray.

ShowConfig.description: How many pipeline rows a watch contributes.

jobs.description:
Which jobs this watch's rows list, overriding `ui.jobs` for this watch
alone. Absent means "whatever `ui.jobs` says"; see
[`Watch::effective_jobs`].

max_rows.description: Hard ceiling on rows for this watch.

settled.description:
How many already-settled pipelines to keep, on top of every unsettled
one. Unsettled pipelines are always shown.

TokenSource.description:
Where a token is read from.

A literal token string is rejected at parse time with an explanatory error:
bridgewatch never wants a credential sitting in a config file.

oneOf.description:
An entry in the OS credential store, addressed exactly as another tool
wrote it. `user` may be empty: `glab` stores its token with an empty
account on the macOS Keychain and an empty `username` attribute on the
Linux Secret Service.

service.description: The credential store's service / collection name.

user.description: The account / username attribute. The empty string is valid.

oneOf.description: An environment variable holding the token.

A program to run; the first line of its stdout, trimmed, is the token.
A non-zero exit is an error.

bridgewatch's own credential-store entry, `bridgewatch:<account>`,
written by the GUI or by `set_own_token`.

UiConfig.description:
Window and presentation settings. The core reads only `jobs`, to put each
watch's effective mode on the view model; the rest are the GUI shell's, and
they live here so the config file stays the one source.

jobs.description:
Which jobs an expanded pipeline row lists: `all` (every job, grouped by
stage) or `failures` (only what the verdict names). A watch may override
it with `show.jobs`.

launch_at_login.description: Register bridgewatch as a login item.

theme_css.description: Path to a CSS file layered over the built-in theme.

VerdictConfig.description: Optional Rhai hook replacing the built-in icon-state rules.

script.description: Path to a `.rhai` script. `~` is expanded.

script_source.description:
Inline script, which takes precedence over `script`. Mostly for tests
and for the GUI's script editor preview.

Watch.description: One thing to watch: a project, a ref pattern and a set of pipeline sources.

deploy_markers.description:
Job names (or `re:` patterns) whose success means "this deployed".
The first one to succeed wins.

dive.description: Which trigger jobs to walk into, and how deep.

id.description: Stable identifier, used in notifications, `--watch` and the GUI.

jobs.description: Per-job class overrides. Keys are matched in file order, first wins.

notify.description: Which events raise a notification, and how they read.

post_deploy_failure.description: What a blocking failure *after* a successful deploy marker does.

project.description: Numeric project id, or a `group/path` which is URL-encoded for you.

ref.description: Ref pattern: exact (`main`), glob (`pf/*`) or regex (`re:^release/.*$`).

role.description: Whether this watch drives the tray icon.

sibling_failure.description: What a failed sibling bridge does to a watch that otherwise deployed.

sources.description: Pipeline sources to accept. Empty means all of them.
